articles.title: Ventola Projects Installs Immersive Bowling Experience in Ecuador, Marking First South American Project
articles.summary: UK-based Ventola Projects partnered with US firm Evogence to deliver ball-responsive projection technology across bowling lanes at PlayGo Entertainment in Cuenca, Ecuador. The installation represents a growing trend of immersive overlays transforming traditional bowling into a premium entertainment experience. FEC operators should take note as immersive bowling continues to expand internationally as a key revenue driver.

articles.title: Supercharged Entertainment Sets Opening Target for Massive Multi-Attraction Venue at Polaris
articles.summary: Supercharged Entertainment has announced a target opening date for its large-scale entertainment venue at the Polaris development, adding another major competitor to the growing large-format FEC market. The venue is expected to feature a wide mix of competitive socializing and amusement attractions. Operators in the region should monitor the opening closely as it signals intensifying competition in the out-of-home entertainment space.

articles.title: Slick City and Activeon Accelerate European Expansion with New Parks in Sweden and Austria
articles.summary: Slick City, the indoor slide and active entertainment concept, is expanding into Europe through a partnership with Activeon, with new parks planned for Sweden and Austria. The move signals growing international appetite for active FEC formats beyond trampolines and laser tag. FEC operators and investors should watch this expansion as a bellwether for which attraction formats are gaining traction in new markets.

articles.title: Fun Spot America to Auction Atlanta Park Equipment Following Permanent Closure
articles.summary: Fun Spot America's Atlanta location, which permanently closed in August 2026, will hold an equipment and asset auction on October 14, offering a wide range of amusement park inventory. This presents a potential buying opportunity for FEC operators looking to acquire rides and equipment at reduced cost. The closure also serves as a cautionary case study for operators evaluating standalone amusement park viability in competitive markets.

articles.title: Major Kansas City Entertainment Center Closes After 13 Years
articles.summary: A large entertainment center in Kansas City has permanently closed after 13 years of operation, with locals expressing strong nostalgia for the venue. The closure highlights ongoing challenges facing legacy FEC operations as consumer preferences and competitive dynamics shift. Operators should consider what this means for venue reinvestment cycles and the importance of regular concept refreshes.

articles.title: Indoor Entertainment Fuels UAE Attractions Boom
articles.summary: The UAE is experiencing a significant boom in indoor entertainment, driven by major IP-based attractions including Harry Potter and Disney concepts, as well as a favorable climate that makes indoor venues especially attractive year-round. The trend reflects growing consumer demand for premium, climate-controlled entertainment experiences across the Gulf region. Suppliers and developers looking to expand internationally should view the UAE as a high-priority growth market.

articles.title: UAE Indoor Entertainment Boom Driven by Major IP Attractions
articles.summary: A market analysis highlights the rapid expansion of indoor entertainment in the UAE, anchored by high-profile IP attractions from Harry Potter and Disney franchises. The report underscores the region's investment in large-scale, experiential indoor venues as alternatives to outdoor theme parks. FEC investors and developers can use this data to benchmark international growth opportunities.

articles.title: accesso's Lee Cowie on AI, Data, and the Future of Attractions Technology
articles.summary: accesso executive Lee Cowie discusses how AI and advanced data analytics are moving attractions technology well beyond basic ticketing into guest experience personalization and in-park revenue optimization. The piece outlines how operators can leverage integrated platforms to reduce friction at every guest touchpoint. For FEC operators, this signals that technology investment in data and AI is becoming a competitive necessity, not a luxury.

articles.title: The Strategic Case for In-Visit AI at Attractions
articles.summary: A new analysis argues that the attractions industry is over-indexing on pre- and post-visit AI applications such as chatbots and analytics, while neglecting the high-value in-visit window when guests are on-site and most receptive to upselling. The piece contends that real-time AI tools could significantly lift secondary spend on food, retail, and premium experiences. FEC operators with flat attendance but growing revenue ambitions should consider in-visit AI as a priority technology investment.

articles.title: InPark Magazine Issue 111 Focuses on Frictionless Guest Experiences and Emerging Technology
articles.summary: The latest issue of InPark Magazine centers on the theme of frictionless guest experiences, covering ticketing innovation, AI integration, and how technology can remove barriers between guests and entertainment. Contributors include accesso, Jora Vision, and Alterface, offering multiple operator perspectives. FEC professionals will find this issue a valuable resource for understanding where technology investment is heading across the broader attractions industry.

articles.title: Jora Vision Expands Competitive Socializing Portfolio with New Interactive Game Concept
articles.summary: Jora Vision is growing its competitive socializing offering, expanding beyond themed design into interactive game attractions where every guest skill level is engaged. The move reflects the broader industry shift toward active, skill-based entertainment as a primary FEC draw. Operators evaluating their attraction mix should consider how competitive socializing formats can drive repeat visitation and group bookings.

articles.title: India's Amusement Industry Posts Summer 2026 Growth but Rising Costs Squeeze Margins
articles.summary: India's amusement sector saw strong attendance growth during summer 2026, but operators are facing increasing pressure from rising operational costs that are eroding profitability. The trend mirrors challenges seen in other global markets where post-pandemic demand has been offset by inflation in labor, energy, and equipment costs. FEC operators worldwide can draw parallels to their own cost management strategies as margin pressure becomes a defining industry challenge.

articles.title: IAAPI Urges Indian Government to Rationalize GST Rates for Amusement Industry
articles.summary: The Indian Association of Amusement Parks and Industries is calling on the government to reduce and rationalize Goods and Services Tax rates applied to amusement venues, arguing current rates suppress consumer demand and hinder industry growth. The advocacy effort highlights how tax policy can be a significant headwind for FEC-style businesses in developing markets. International operators and investors evaluating India should factor regulatory and tax environments into their market entry assessments.

articles.title: Deutsche Bank Cuts Hollywood Bowl Target Price as Summer Heatwave Dents Indoor Footfall
articles.summary: Deutsche Bank has lowered its price target for UK bowling and entertainment operator Hollywood Bowl after a summer heatwave reduced indoor footfall, underscoring how weather events can materially impact FEC revenue. The analyst note is a reminder that even well-run indoor entertainment businesses are not immune to external environmental factors. FEC operators and investors should consider weather-driven demand volatility when modeling revenue forecasts.

articles.title: Efteling and TU Delft Launch SafeStrap to Enable Roller Coaster Access for Guests with Leg Prostheses
articles.summary: Efteling theme park partnered with Delft University of Technology and a rehabilitation center to develop SafeStrap, a device that allows guests with leg prostheses to ride roller coasters without removing them. The innovation directly advances accessibility and inclusion at amusement attractions, broadening the potential guest base. FEC operators should monitor SafeStrap's adoption as consumer and regulatory expectations around attraction accessibility continue to rise.

articles.title: Texas' Largest Family Entertainment Center Coming to Houston in 2026
articles.summary: A new FEC claiming to be the largest in Texas is set to open in Houston in 2026, featuring an extensive mix of indoor attractions. The scale of the project reflects continued investor confidence in large-format FEC development in high-population markets. Operators and developers tracking the competitive landscape in Texas should closely follow this venue's opening and initial performance.

articles.title: Launch Family Fun Center Bringing Arcade and Trampoline Park to Pensacola's Davis Highway
articles.summary: Launch Family Entertainment is opening a new multi-attraction complex on Davis Highway in Pensacola, Florida, featuring trampoline parks, arcades, and other active entertainment offerings. The venue is part of Launch's broader national expansion strategy, adding another market to its growing footprint. Local and regional FEC operators should note Launch's continued growth as a sign of strong consumer demand for multi-attraction indoor entertainment.

articles.title: New Indoor FEC Coming to LaPorte with Bowling, Mini-Golf, Arcade, and More
articles.summary: A new indoor family entertainment center is planned for LaPorte, Indiana, combining bowling, mini-golf, arcade gaming, and additional attractions under one roof. The multi-concept approach mirrors a growing industry trend of bundling complementary entertainment formats to maximize dwell time and per-capita spending. This opening is a useful benchmark for operators evaluating the viability of diversified FEC models in mid-sized markets.

articles.title: New Indoor Family Entertainment Center Opens in Mt. Juliet Over Labor Day Weekend
articles.summary: A new indoor FEC debuted in Mt. Juliet, Tennessee over the Labor Day weekend, capitalizing on a high-traffic holiday period to drive initial awareness and attendance. The timing reflects a common and effective launch strategy for FEC operators looking to build early momentum. The opening adds to a wave of new FEC entrants across the southeastern United States.

articles.title: Dream Garden Creates Custom Multi-Level FEC for KIDDO Venue in Venezuela
articles.summary: Chinese manufacturer Dream Garden delivered a fully customized, multi-level family entertainment environment for KIDDO at Centro San Ignacio in Caracas, combining active play, physical challenges, and themed elements within a compact commercial footprint. The project highlights growing demand for bespoke FEC design in Latin American markets beyond cookie-cutter playground installations. Operators and designers looking for differentiation through customization will find this case study instructive.

articles.title: Six Flags and Warner Bros. Invest in Premium Interactive Horror with The Conjuring: Beyond Fear
articles.summary: Six Flags is partnering with Plague Productions and Warner Bros. Discovery Global Experiences to launch The Conjuring: Beyond Fear, a premium interactive horror attraction targeting the lucrative Halloween season. The investment signals a shift toward higher-ticket, deeply immersive seasonal experiences as operators look to extract more revenue per guest during fall. FEC operators with Halloween programming should assess how premium interactive horror formats could elevate their own seasonal event strategies.

articles.title: InPark Editorial: Removing Friction Is the Central Challenge for Attraction Operators
articles.summary: InPark Magazine's publisher argues that reducing friction across every guest touchpoint, from ticketing to in-park purchasing to experience access, is the defining operational priority for attractions today. The editorial frames technology not as a novelty but as a tool fundamentally serving the guest experience. FEC operators should use this framing to audit where friction points are costing them revenue and guest satisfaction.

articles.title: Avoiding the Resolution Trap: What Actually Matters When Buying an Immersive Attraction
articles.summary: An experienced supplier challenges the industry habit of specifying immersive attractions purely by resolution figures like 8K, arguing that brightness, contrast in real operating environments, and long-term image quality maintenance matter far more for guest experience. The piece offers practical guidance for operators writing RFPs for dome theatres, flying theatres, and immersive spaces. FEC buyers considering immersive visual attractions will benefit from this technical perspective before committing capital.

articles.title: Alterface Celebrates 25 Years of Designing Interactive Themed Entertainment Experiences
articles.summary: Interactive experience design firm Alterface marks its 25th anniversary by reflecting on its legacy of creating what it calls 'invisible magic,' where technology enhances guest engagement without overshadowing the story. The company's portfolio spans interactive dark rides and shooting attractions at major theme parks worldwide. FEC operators exploring interactive dark ride or shooting gallery formats should be familiar with Alterface's capabilities and design philosophy.

articles.title: Out-of-Home Advertising Remains a Powerful Tool for Last-Minute Entertainment Decision-Makers
articles.summary: New research shows that today's entertainment consumers are increasingly making day-of decisions about where to go, shrinking the pre-visit window and making out-of-home advertising like billboards and posters more valuable for driving spontaneous visits. A post-show survey found OOH was the fifth-largest source of audience awareness, outperforming TV and TikTok in driving discovery. FEC operators relying heavily on digital pre-booking campaigns should consider how OOH placements near their venues can capture last-minute foot traffic.

articles.title: WildBrain CPLG to Drive Miraculous Location-Based Entertainment Opportunities Across EMEA and APAC
articles.summary: Licensing agency WildBrain CPLG has been appointed to develop location-based entertainment opportunities for the Miraculous animated brand across Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia-Pacific. The deal signals growing interest from IP holders in expanding into FEC and attraction settings beyond traditional retail licensing. FEC operators seeking branded IP partnerships should be aware of Miraculous as an emerging option with strong appeal among children and families.

articles.title: Attraktion! Installs Full Product Catalogue at Polish Adventure Park
articles.summary: European attractions supplier Attraktion! has completed a comprehensive multi-product installation at a Polish adventure park, showcasing its full range of active attractions in a single venue. The project demonstrates the growing appetite for active outdoor and indoor adventure formats across Central and Eastern Europe. FEC operators evaluating active attraction suppliers should take note of Attraktion!'s expanding European track record.

articles.title: IAAPA Expo Europe 2026 Preview: Key Speakers, Exhibitors, and Industry Trends to Watch
articles.summary: IAAPA Expo Europe returns to London's ExCeL from September 21-25, 2026, bringing together attractions industry leaders to showcase innovations in ride systems, immersive experiences, operations, and guest engagement. The UK attractions market is forecast to grow 9.8% through 2027, outpacing the European average, making this year's event especially significant. FEC operators, suppliers, and investors planning to attend should use this preview to prioritize which exhibitors and sessions align with their business goals.

articles.title: Fresno's Empty Bed Bath & Beyond Converted into New Entertainment Venue
articles.summary: A vacant Bed Bath & Beyond retail space in Fresno, California is being repurposed as a new entertainment center, reflecting the ongoing trend of FEC operators backfilling former big-box retail locations. The conversion model continues to offer attractive economics for FEC developers, with large floor plates, high-visibility retail locations, and favorable lease terms from landlords eager to fill vacancies. Operators and developers should monitor the Fresno project as a case study in retail-to-FEC conversion.

articles.title: Pomvom Appoints Deborah Eicher as VP of Global Sales to Drive Theme Park and Attraction Revenue Growth
articles.summary: AI-powered guest experience technology company Pomvom has hired Deborah Eicher, a 20-year industry veteran, as VP of Global Sales and Business Development, with a mandate to expand partnerships across theme parks, attractions, and entertainment destinations worldwide. The appointment signals Pomvom's intent to accelerate commercial growth as AI-driven content and guest experience tools gain traction in the sector. FEC technology buyers should expect increased outreach from Pomvom as it scales its sales operation.
